# v2.97-dev

Two hardening changes to how the system handles text that came from outside it —
a web address typed into a link field, and a value that ends up in an exported
spreadsheet.

## Fixed

- **A training or offering link is now checked before it is saved.** These
  fields accept a web address, and until now they accepted anything at all.
  They now take ordinary `http://` and `https://` addresses and nothing else.
  Saving something else tells you why rather than quietly storing it, and a
  spreadsheet import reports the rows it could not accept and carries on with
  the rest.

  Anything already saved that is not a web address is no longer shown as a
  clickable link, so existing data is covered without anyone having to go and
  find it. This is a precaution rather than a repair: testing in a real browser
  confirmed that such a link already did nothing when clicked. The check means
  the system no longer depends on the browser for that, and that these values
  are not handed on to anything reading them through the API.

- **Exported CSV files can no longer smuggle a spreadsheet formula.** A
  spreadsheet treats a value starting with certain characters as a formula to
  run rather than text to show, so a name or title that merely passed through
  the system could take effect in the spreadsheet of whoever opened the file.
  Those values are now marked as text.

  This matters most for **scheduled exports**, which write files to a shared
  drive on a timer with nobody there to notice anything unusual before the file
  is opened.

  Ordinary content is unchanged — including negative numbers and percentages,
  which are still exported exactly as before — and Excel exports were already
  unaffected, so they are untouched.

## Upgrading

No action needed, and nothing to reconfigure. Existing exports and saved links
keep working.
